chunks: I am the axis of the mill,
It rotates on me while I remain in my position,
As soon as I leave it the centre of its rotation would be disturbed and its lower stone would also be disturbed.
By Allāh, this is a very bad advice.
By Allāh, if I had not been hoping for martyrdom by my meeting with the enemy—and my meeting with him has been ordained,
I would have secured my carrier and went away from you
and would not have sought you so long as North and South differed.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Imam Ali's metaphor of the mill's axis in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of the 'axis of the mill' (Qutb al-Rahā) to illustrate his indispensable role as the central pillar maintaining the stability and order of the community; without him, the 'millstone' of governance would spin chaotically. He clarifies that his continued presence among the people was not out of attachment to power, but driven by the hope of martyrdom in battle, noting that had it not been for this expectation, he would have departed so completely that they would not have found him even if they searched from east to west.
